And Sultan Muhammad
had left one hundred and twenty thousand warriors, men, in it for its protection.
Now when Genghis Khan heard
that it was so strong in fighters,
he himself went in person against it.
And the Mongols surrounded it,
and counted its towers,
and the fire of war was kindled between those inside and those outside upon the wall.
And on the next day, the forces inside went out in a sally against the Tatars,
and they fought fierce battles,
and they killed many of the Tatars,
and took others alive,
and brought them into the city,
and tortured them,
and killed them cruelly.
Now the citizens, when they saw this, were very afraid,
and said to one another:
"The vengeance for these will surely come upon us, if we are negligent."
And they took counsel together,
and sent some men secretly to Genghis
Khan,
and promised to open the gates by night
and surrender the city.
And Genghis Khan rejoiced at this,
and gave his word for their lives.
And when evening came,
the judge (qadi) of the city and another who was called Shaykh al-Islam assembled
a large gathering of the common folk,
and they opened the gates of the city,
and the Mongols entered it.
And the fighters belonging to the city fled and took refuge in the citadel.
And the Tatars began to take captive and to plunder.
And the people of the city,
men and women,
they brought out outside the city by hundreds,
and made them sit in separate groups,
except for fifty thousand who were spared with the judge and Shaykh al-Islam and did not go outside.
And when night fell,
the Tatars went out
and killed all those whom they had brought outside,
and did not spare [any]
except only boys and girls under twenty years of age.
Now one of the commanders who was in the citadel performed a great act of bravery:
he took about a thousand men,
and cleaved the forces of the Tatars and passed between them,
and they fled (or: he fled) —
for they were not able to withstand his swiftness —
and he went to Khorasan to Sultan Muhammad.
[Of the campaign of the] Tatars to Khwarazm.
Genghis
Khan, however, when he had finished with the affair of Samarkand,
sent both his sons Chagatai and Ogedei against Khwarazm.
